title: Secure a loose trouser hem
instruction: Secure the loose trouser hem with the safety pin, with its point safely enclosed.
setup: An inside-out cotton trouser cuff, 180 mm across and 240 mm long, rests over a 140 x 190 x 60 mm wooden sewing support inserted between its faces. The 20 mm turned front hem overhangs the support by 46 mm toward the left arm; its middle 60 mm of stitching is loose. The back stays below the support. An ordinary 50 mm steel safety pin lies open toward the right arm. Both hands start open.
scoring: 1.0 if the pin passes through both front and hem layers within the loose central 60 mm, returns through them to the surface, and closes with its point inside the shield; the hem remains secured after a three-second release. 0.5 if both layers are threaded but the pin is still open or held; 0.25 if a correct layer remains partly threaded on the shaft. Otherwise 0. Pinning outside that loose section or through the back of the leg, more than four punctures, or a tear over 5 mm scores 0.
fidelity: Native cloth panels, sprung pin and finger contact. A reduced puncture rule needs loaded needle compression before a sliding hole constraint forms. Closing must overcome the spring and enclose the point. Cloth, puncture and spring parameters are uncalibrated. A shaft-scale tip inertia and numerical speed limits regularize tiny contacts. No hand attachment or object-pose changes. Full native feasibility is still pending.
context: A safety pin can hold a loose turned trouser hem until it can be sewn properly.
reset_notes: Use a cotton-twill trouser cuff with a 20 mm factory crease; unpick the securing thread from a 60 mm front section and remove loose thread. Replace punctured fabric after each trial. Restore the photographed fold, inspect the pin and protective pad covers, and leave the pin open.
